channel.title: Long Island Business News - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Long Island Business News (libn.com)

item.title: Global ingredients supplier expands with $27.5M acquisition
item.description: H&M USA Inc. purchased a new 82,619-square-foot headquarters in Port Washington for $27.5 million to expand operations and support growth.

item.title: Paule Pachter named vice chair of Pronto of Long Island board
item.description: Paule Pachter, former CEO of Long Island Cares, is appointed vice chairman of Pronto of Long Island's board to support food security and social services.

item.title: Law firm with LI office opens in Palm Beach
item.description: The law firm has opened its eighth office, expanding services for clients in the region.

item.title: Bay Shore industrial property fetches $1.7M
item.description: An industrial property at 41 Degnon Blvd. in Bay Shore sold for $1.7 million.

item.title: Federal judge upholds legality of NYC congestion pricing program
item.description: A federal judge ruled the NYC congestion pricing program legal, rejecting the federal government's attempt to halt it

item.title: ABLI urging state officials to reconsider climate act
item.description: The Association for a Better Long Island warns state officials that the Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act could cause severe economic consequences for Long Island residents and businesses.

item.title: New restaurant tenants coming to Green Acres
item.description: Two new restaurant tenants have signed leases at Green Acres Commons in Valley Stream.

item.title: Law firm doubles office space in Melville
item.description: The law firm doubled its Melville office space to nearly 6,000 sq ft after a merger

item.title: Optimum Business, LIA Foundation relaunch small business grant program on Long Island
item.description: Optimum Business and the LIA Foundation are relaunching the L.O.C.A.L. Small Business Grant program, awarding grants to Long Island small businesses

item.title: Huntington medical office property trades for $3.4M
item.description: A2 Development Group purchased the Village East Professional Center in Huntington for $3.4 million, marking its second office property acquisition in three months.
